items.title: Push-to-Talk (PTT) Mode
items.description: Manual transmission by push button. Press and hold the Talk button to open the microphone channel and start capturing real-time audio. When you release it, the transmission ends immediately and the system processes the transcription automatically.
items.note: Recommended for environments with high noise or situations where precise control of communication is required.

items.title: Automatic Mode (Volume Detection)
items.description: Automatic transmission based on input signal level. The system activates audio capture when it detects sound above the configured sensitivity threshold and stops recording after a brief period of silence.
items.note: Ideal for a completely hands-free experience.

items.description: It is recommended to connect any type of device (either Bluetooth headphones/microphones or external sound cards) **before starting the server or application**. items.title: Spoken Numbers to Digits Conversion
items.description: Allows AI to transcribe spoken numerical expressions directly as figures instead of words (e.g. '12' instead of 'twelve', '-6 dB' instead of 'minus six decibels').
items.note: Highly recommended to speed up reading channels, cues, and live technical levels.

items.title: Babel Translation Engine
items.description: The system integrates Babel, an optimized neural machine translation (NMT) engine that runs 100% locally on the Master Server. Translate messages received in other languages ​​in real time into the language of your interface without sending data to the Internet or depending on external APIs.

items.title: Offline Voice Reading
items.description: Allows automated reading of incoming text messages or translations. It exclusively uses the native voice engine of your operating system (Web Speech API), operating 100% locally, privately and without requiring the internet. Its disk consumption is 0 bytes and it has a practically zero impact on CPU/RAM.

items.title: Adjustable and Individual Parameters
items.description: Configure the functionality according to your preferences from the Settings tab of your device:
subitems: Listen to text messages: Activate the reading of local texts. If it is turned off, your language texts will remain silent but you will still be able to hear foreign translations.
Foreign Audio Filter: Blocks original audios in other languages and only reads their translation.

Reaction to Active Filters: The system reads only incoming messages that correspond to the category or channel selected by the user in their chat filters (if filtered by a specific group, it will only read those from that group; if 'All' is selected, it will read them all).
Voice Selection: Choose from the available voices installed on your operating system, or leave it on Automatic to inherit the app's language.
Gender Filter: Dynamically filters compatible voices according to their tone (Male, Female or All).
Reading Speed: Adjusts the pace of speech between extremely slow (0.5x) and fast (2.0x).

items.title: Prefixes and Context Introductions
items.description: The narrator automatically detects the type of message for a more natural reading: it will say '[Name] wrote...' for pure text messages, and '[Name] said...' when playing voice message translations.

items.title: Shield of Coexistence (Hermes-Shield)
items.description: To avoid acoustic coupling with the microphone and not interfere with fluid communication, Hermes TTS will automatically mute itself if:
subitems: You are pressing the Talk button or recording with your microphone.
There is active playback in the chat's native audio queue.
Any child HTML5 media player in the DOM is active.

items.title: Smart Localized Prefixes
items.description: Before reading the message, a dynamic prefix is automatically synthesized according to the active language to provide context about the sender (for example: 'Jorge has written: [message]' or 'Jorge has written: [message]').

items.title: Local Persistence
items.description: All settings are stored independently for each user in the terminal's localStorage. Changing your voice or speed options will not affect other users on the local network or other profiles logged in in the same browser.

items.title: Deployment Scheme (Step by Step)
items.description: To configure this infrastructure correctly, follow these professional guidelines:
subitems: 1. Running the Master Server: Start the Talk-me server on the main computer (Master). This must have an active license.
2. Obtaining the Local IP: Find out the private IP address of the server (ex: 192.168.1.150).

3. Wired Client Connection (Ethernet): Connect the support computers using a network cable (RJ45 Cat6 recommended) to the router or switch. Access by opening the browser at https://192.168.1.150:3000.
4. Connecting Clients via Wi-Fi (Mobiles / Tablets): Make sure that phones and tablets are connected to the Wi-Fi network issued by the same router. Open the same URL in your mobile device's browser.

items.title: Browser Security Requirements (Camera and Microphone)
items.description: Modern browsers restrict access to sensitive devices such as cameras and microphones when the connection is not secure.
items.important: For this reason, access to the system must be done using HTTPS, accepting the self-signed local SSL certificate generated by the server during installation.

items.title: Complete Sovereignty and Cloud Independence
items.description: Talk-me has been designed to operate 100% autonomously within your network infrastructure. Once installed, it does not require a permanent Internet connection or third-party APIs. If WAN (Internet) access is cut, internal campus communication, translation, local transcription and alerts will continue to operate without interruption.
